concerns.text: The plan falls back to generating synthetic WCST data and placeholder nostalgia stimuli when no real dataset is found. Synthetic data cannot provide evidence about a real associational link between nostalgia exposure and cognitive flexibility, so the primary research question cannot be answered with empirical validity.

No a priori power analysis is presented. The synthetic dataset size (200 participants, 100 per condition) is chosen arbitrarily; without a power calculation the study may be under‑powered to detect realistic effect sizes, making the MDES post‑hoc estimate insufficient for design justification.

Confound control is limited to optional covariate adjustment that is only applied if extra variables happen to exist. Key potential confounds (e.g., education, gender, health status, within‑group age variation) are not planned to be measured or adjusted, threatening internal validity.

Placeholder stimulus files are marked “simulation only” and are not validated as genuine nostalgia‑inducing material. Without a validated manipulation, the construct of “nostalgia exposure” is not operationalized, compromising construct validity of the independent variable.
